Method of Attack: Installing a root certificate into the Trusted Root CA Certificate store with the same private key for all installations, allowing attackers to decrypt the private key and issue fraudulent certificates for man-in-the-middle attacks
Use of an encrypted private key with AES-128-CBC encryption stored insecurely in WBCCListener.dll and WBCCServer.properties files
Persistent trusted root certificate remains after software uninstall, enabling continued attacks
Impacted Systems: Computers with Sennheiser HeadSetup software installed
Attack Vector: Installation of software that places root certificates and private keys on the system
Decryption of private key using stored encryption key and passphrase in software files
Use of fraudulent certificates to intercept and alter TLS traffic
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of root certificate SennComCCCert.pem in Trusted Root CA store
Presence of private key file SennComCCKey.pem
Files WBCCListener.dll and WBCCServer.properties containing encryption key and passphrase
Certificates issued for domains such as google.com, sennheiser.com, jbl.com, harmankardon.com, bose.com
